docs.title: Echopy for FontLab
docs.text:
Use FontLab's native Python API with source-readable definitions, annotations, and enriched documentation. fontlab_echopy and echopy share the same modules.

from echopy import fontlab as fl, fontgate as fg, fontpr
node = fl.flNode(12, 34)  # Inside FontLab: the original native flNode.

Install the wheel into a Python directory on FontLab's interpreter path. Python 3.11 or newer is required. No PySide2 runtime is installed into FontLab.

uv pip install dist/fontlab_echopy-*.whl
# From this checkout, including generation/enrichment dependencies:
uv sync --extra test --extra enrich

Generation checks native-to-Python name mappings before writing output. If two spellings would become the same declaration, it raises a collision error naming the owner and spellings; it does not replace an existing output tree with partial results. The preflight also refuses top-level names mapping to Any, globals, _bind, _unavailable, _echopy_native, _echopy_name, _echopy_aliases or _echopy_unavailable, which are used by generated facades. It covers these conflicts, not every possible write failure or every reserved-name interaction.

Generated static/class method decorators use a private builtins alias selected to avoid captured module and class-member names, including normalized spellings. Captured names such as staticmethod and classmethod remain exposed. This protects the generated declarations without adding those names to the refusal list; merged runtime facades remain lazy. Native capture/refresh is a separate gate.

docs.title: Documentation map
docs.text: Read installation, declarations and tooling, development and limits, and component licences.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Echopy shims only FontLab's native bindings: fontlab, fontgate, fontpr, fontlabpr (absent in measured builds; the absence is recorded) and FL and PythonQt.*. It does not emulate other APIs. The FL module (FontLab 5 compatibility, from FL import *) is shipped as fontlab_echopy.FL (136 names, 30 classes, from a native FontLab 9 capture). To refresh it, run tools/capture_fl.py in a checkout with fontlab-remopy (read-only, several short host calls), then generate and merge. The raw capture JSON stays local, like the other captures.

Packages that earlier releases generated here now belong to their producers: GlyphsApp, vanilla, AppKit, Cocoa, Foundation, objc to fontlab-glyport, fontlabapp_shim to fontlab-fontlabapp and aidus_code_tools to fontlab-aidus-code. fontlab_echopy.<name> for those raises ImportError naming the new home.

The Issue 123 branch's GlyphsApp manager, profile and provenance notes describe those moved shims; they now belong with fontlab-glyport.

docs.title: Extensions and immutable classes
docs.text:
from fontlab_echopy.extensions import layer_names, has_layer, install_extensions
names = layer_names(glyph)
status = install_extensions()

The layer helpers work on original native objects. Installation adds only absent methods to mutable native classes and reports immutable classes explicitly. Maintained patch bodies are compiled into _patch_extensions.py by merge; installation reads that generated registry. For any immutable class, use get_extension("fontlab.flGlyph.layer_names")(glyph) to call its patch directly. In the tested host, flGlyph cannot receive convenience methods, while QWidget accepts echopy_object_name. The standalone helpers remain available in both cases. Existing native methods are never replaced by convenience fallbacks.

docs.title: Document the actual native names
docs.text:
The enriched Python source is also the documentation authority for the live fontlab, fontgate, fontpr, optional fontlabpr and PythonQt.* namespaces. Capture inside FontLab first, then generate/enrich/merge outside it. Qt HTML becomes structured Markdown docstrings: paragraphs, lists, links, tables and code examples remain readable in the generated Python sidecars.

fontlab-echopy docnames /path/to/documentation/.build/native-names

This exports explicit Python aliases, with source/output SHA-256 provenance, instead of copying declarations. Configure the mkdocstrings Python handler with that directory and Echopy's source/install directory in paths, allow_inspection: false, and preload_modules: [fontlab_echopy]. Then ::: fontlab.flNode documents the actual native name from the enriched source. Keep these aliases on the documentation loader path; the live runtime continues to use FontLab's original objects.

Use the Griffe extension fontlab_echopy.tooling.griffe_native.NativeNamespaceExtension in the handler's options.extensions. It preserves native classes such as PythonQt.BoolResult whose empty pseudo-namespace would otherwise shadow their class declaration. The alias manifest retains that namespace's source evidence. No native import or method invocation is required to build the reference.

Code-shadow-derived code uses Apache-2.0. Qt reference documentation retains GFDL-1.3 and PySide2 declarations LGPL-3.0 terms. See NOTICE and licenses/. The legacy Aidus introspector retains its original proprietary license and is archived only; it is not part of either installable distribution.

docs.title: Regeneration
docs.text:
The inputs and outputs are independent:

  • generated/: raw source generated from native metadata.
  • patches/manual.json: maintained docs, typing, and explicit extensions.
  • enrichment/qt5.json: fetched and parsed upstream documentation/signatures.
  • src/fontlab_echopy/: merged, installable output and supporting runtime/tools.
  • reports/: native coverage and upstream URLs, hashes and coverage gaps.
  • legacy/: verbatim migration archive, including generators, overlays and RST documentation. It is excluded from wheels and source distributions.

Discovery unions advertised names with direct namespace dictionary keys, retaining public API names hidden by a custom __dir__. PythonQt child discovery also uses a snapshot of loaded module names and qualified imports for children absent from root attributes. Root objects take precedence over registry/import objects; nested registry paths identify their immediate child. Ordinary discovery failures remain explicit in capture and generation reports; an absent optional child is distinguished from a missing dependency. Failed root getters are not retried, and execution deadlines/interrupts propagate. This tooling repair does not refresh the retained captures or establish native completeness. Existing native capture and publication holds remain applicable.

First run examples/capture_in_fontlab.py inside FontLab. It writes an API-only capture to your user cache, with no member limits and no method calls. Captures are local inputs, not distribution contents. Then, from this checkout:

fontlab-echopy generate ~/.cache/fontlab-echopy/native.json generated
fontlab-echopy enrich ~/.cache/fontlab-echopy/native.json enrichment/qt5.json \
  --cache .cache/upstream
fontlab-echopy merge generated src/fontlab_echopy \
  --overlay enrichment/qt5.json --overlay patches/manual.json

The repeatable one-command equivalent captures inside FontLab if --capture is omitted. Outside FontLab, supply a previously captured file:

fontlab-echopy pipeline --capture ~/.cache/fontlab-echopy/native.json \
  --raw generated --output src/fontlab_echopy --qt-cache .cache/upstream \
  --qt-overlay enrichment/qt5.json --overlay patches/manual.json --reports reports

The pipeline also writes _identities.json into the merged package: every captured scope, name, class member and constructor, the capture hash, the native spelling of each sanitized identity (QPainter::PixmapFragment → QPainter__PixmapFragment, QWidget.raise → QWidget.raise_), maintained extensions, unmatched overlay targets and enrichment gaps. Documentation builds reconcile their coverage against it without the raw capture. To refresh or check it against a capture without regenerating sidecars:

fontlab-echopy identities path/to/native.json src/fontlab_echopy
fontlab-echopy verify-identities path/to/native.json src/fontlab_echopy

Both refuse a capture other than the generation input recorded in _provenance.json, and fail when two native names map to one source name.

The pipeline never edits overlays. Regenerating raw output also leaves merged output untouched until merge. Manual overlays take precedence over upstream material. Unmatched overlay targets are reported instead of silently counted. The CLI accepts older pseudopackages_api_docs.json captures as well. Host execution deadlines propagate as errors. Large captures should run from FontLab’s scripting surface; MCP users must split introspection into bounded namespace calls to respect its fixed execution deadline.

Qt enrichment queries official PyPI for the latest PySide2 release, downloads one wheel for architecture-independent .pyi extraction, checks its SHA256, then fetches official Qt 5 class/member documentation. It intersects native names and includes QtWidgets definitions under PythonQt.QtGui where present. Downloads stay in the supplied cache. All matching classes are processed by default; enrich --max-classes N is only for limited experiments, recorded in the coverage report. PySide6 needs separate Qt6 mappings and native Qt-version checks; changing the package name alone would not be a valid transition.

docs.title: Verification and building
docs.text:
./test.sh
uv build
# Inside FontLab against the installed wheel:
# execute examples/native_smoke.py

Versioning uses Git tags through hatch-vcs. WORK.md records local checks; CHANGELOG.md records delivered behavior. MIGRATION.json retains source revision/file hashes, including uncommitted source, and accounts for excluded build/cache artifacts. Source originals have not been removed.

Griffe (also used by mkdocstrings) resolves the canonical source and stub pairs:

import griffe
api = griffe.load("fontlab_echopy", allow_inspection=False, prefer_stubs_docs=True)
print(api.get_member("PythonQt.QtGui.QWidget.resize").docstring.value)

Source-only consumers that ignore .pyi files see the runtime facade; configure stub support as above to retain the complete enriched documentation.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Issue 101 migration is complete and released as verified v0.2.0 (RELEASE.md): source and licence provenance, capture of every native namespace and PythonQt child, the capture/generate/enrich/merge pipeline, native-identity facades with .pyi sidecars, PySide2/Qt 5 enrichment with coverage reports, deterministic regeneration, and installed-wheel checks in FontLab.

v0.2.1 to v0.2.3 added generator-v3 static shims for Glyphs, Cocoa/vanilla, Aidus and Fontlabapp; issue 201 removed them again (see Scope). They also added structured Qt Markdown and separate overload source lines in enrichment; docnames aliases that let mkdocstrings render the native fontlab/fontgate/fontpr/PythonQt identities; and the BoolResult class/namespace collision handling, each proven by strict source-only rendering. fontlabpr is absent in FontLab 9.0.9780; capture records that absence.

docs.title: Archive preservation in this delivery
docs.text: This remote branch retains legacy/README.md, legacy/source.tar.gz and licenses/aidus-legacy-LICENSE byte-for-byte. A later canonical cleanup does not delete them here. The source/runtime/tooling matches that canonical checkpoint. No generation, native capture, package release or archive removal is part of this variant.

docs.title: Qualification boundary
docs.text: The maintained acd615697 source and ordinary artifact milestone passed 437 tests. Dated README status below remains historical evidence. Native FontLab execution, current-provider capture and owner installation are separate; this site build performs none of those operations. Source capture, enrichment and generation commands above describe maintenance responsibilities, not actions performed by this build. Private Pages configuration and publication remain owner-held.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Use arm64 Python 3.11 for the FontLab host; this documentation build uses Python 3.13. Host installation and native acceptance are separate gates.

docs.title: Runtime contract
docs.text:
Classes, constructors, functions, constants, and results delegate to native objects. fl.flNode is fontlab.flNode and native isinstance/argument conversion keep working. Module attributes remain live; assigning an attribute delegates back to the native namespace. Deleting a native attribute also removes it from facade lookup and dir(); cached declarations do not restore a deleted value. Accepted native names beginning _echopy_ and their sanitized aliases share current native reads, writes and deletion. The three exact internal state names _echopy_native, _echopy_name and _echopy_aliases remain local; child facade installation remains import bookkeeping. Canonical .pyi sidecars contain complete readable class/member declarations, signatures and documentation. Small .py facades bind native symbols without compiling the large documentation source, keeping imports within the host execution deadline. The native classes remain the runtime authority: their __doc__ and inspect.signature are not rewritten.

Outside FontLab, source modules import for documentation. Calling a declared native function or constructing a native class raises NativeUnavailable. Offline imports materialize the sidecar declarations; this costs more time and memory than native imports. Static documentation tools can read them directly. Native-valued attributes are annotated but cannot be read outside the host. Top-level native spellings that are Python keywords or contain punctuation have sanitized source aliases in newly generated declarations, including functions and annotated values. Inside the host, alias reads, writes and deletes use the original native spelling and follow later native reassignment. Outside the host, annotation-only values remain absent; aliases do not invent placeholder values. Existing merged facades retain their alias mappings. This tooling repair still requires a reviewed capture/generated refresh and native acceptance.

New generation also retains captured documentation for module-level annotated attributes, constants and namespaces. Maintained overlays can supply their docs and type through the declared Python identifier, including a sanitized alias. Those declarations remain annotation-only outside FontLab. This tooling repair does not refresh the existing native captures or generated reference.

Unknown signatures deliberately use annotated *args, **kwargs. PySide2 reference overloads are labeled as upstream signatures because PythonQt calling conventions differ. Only unanimous primitive types strengthen native signatures.

Generation preserves a single captured constructor signature and its documentation. Explicit Python static/class constructors retain their descriptor binding and unbound signatures, including inherited constructors. No constructor is invoked during capture. Known Python instance methods and constructors retain their actual receiver name; generation does not add self when that receiver is spelled differently. Unknown native descriptors keep the conservative fallback until their binding is known. Multiple constructor records retain all evidence under a variadic declaration; the generator does not choose an overload. Missing constructor metadata keeps the legacy fallback. This does not qualify constructor behavior in a newer host.

fontpr is captured separately. fontlabpr was absent in the verified host; its facade supports runtime delegation when a future host provides it. No invented fontlabpr API is shipped. PythonQt includes every discovered child, including Config, Debug, private and BoolResult, even when the child cannot be imported as a real Python module. C++ nested/template names have sanitized source aliases; original names remain available through getattr.

docs.text:

  • LICENSE — exact retained legal bytes.

  • Qt-LICENSE.COMMERCIAL — exact retained legal bytes.

Native API facades and the original code-shadow retain Apache 2.0 attribution. Qt reference documentation retains GNU FDL 1.3 attribution; Qt for Python declarations retain LGPLv3 or their original alternative terms. The NOTICE records those source distinctions. The proprietary legacy introspector remains private and excluded from distributions; neither its body nor its private archive is compiled into this site. Existing provenance reports and their frozen source identities remain unchanged.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record binds the retained MaterialX 10.1.8 browser assets to exact upstream notices, package archives and source maps. Product terms above remain unchanged.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. The build rejects theme/search-language, corpus, vendor-set/hash and local HTML-reference drift before removing them. Nine core vendor assets remain byte-identical. Historical complete outputs remain recovery evidence; omitted helpers are not represented as currently distributed or relicensed.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Material Design icons retain the Pictogrammers notice and Apache 2.0 icon terms or specifically stated underlying terms; code is MIT. Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed ordered SVG path tuples, 43 match installed MaterialX icon path tuples exactly, including fontawesome/solid/caret-down.svg used by --md-version-icon. Its unchanged CSS header identifies Font Awesome Free 7.1.0, Copyright 2025 Fonticons, Inc., and CC-BY-4.0 icon terms; the full Font Awesome notice remains available below. The official Font Awesome 7.1.0 NPM caret SVG has different raw path bytes from the installed icon and CSS. The two unmatched Lucide focus/download tuples retain their pinned SCSS attribution. No unchanged-primary SVG, whole-geometry or optimizer-recipe equivalence is claimed.

FontLab's shared theme and external font responses remain external HTTPS services. Their implementation/font bytes are not copied into this payload; reference notices below do not freeze future responses. Build dependencies and local/hosted publication have separate qualification.
